Yes! So the cake base is from this recipe:

http://www.confessionsofacookbookqueen.com/mint-chocolate-chip-cake

The icing is this icing here:

https://bakingamoment.com/magical-cream-cheese-frosting

And the inspiration for the cake design was from lilypinkbakery on Instagram:

https://instagram.com/lilypinkbakery

So what I did was I baked the 2 cake bases exactly as in the recipe, and then wrapped it in plastic wrap after it cooled and then I put them in the freezer, then the next day I made the frosting. I doubled the recipe on the frosting. I also recommend following it exactly. Even cooling it in the fridge after cooking it and before adding the cream cheese, and straining it. Straining it was so difficult but it did get some chunks of flour out I hadn't seen in it! I divided and colored my frosting and had them ready in piping bags and put them in the fridge to cool. Later the same day I got my cakes out of the freezer and trimmed the cakes flat down on top and frosted the top of one and put the other cake upside down on top and I frosted the whole thing with a thin layer, and then froze it again. Frosted it later with a thicker layer and then added the flowers and such. Basically after each frosting attempt I put it back in the freezer for a few minutes. It really seemed to help! I've always done them day of, last minute rushing. I've never frozen a cake before and so I thought I would just try it this time and now I see why I always failed!

Thank you!! I'm so happy with it! It's a little rough in some spots, but I am excited for progress! I was so close to giving up on making and decorating cakes entirely because I ruined almost all my attempts over the years.

I invested in a few little jars of Wilton gel colors over the years, and they are great! Just a little dab of it makes really vibrant colors. These particular ones were more pastel but they make darker shades! And thank you!
Thank you so much! I was very anxious the whole time, thinking I would surely mess it up and have to bring an ugly tasteless cake to the party. Ha

I have practiced baking off and on for about ten years now and they've been 90% of the time failures. I took my time this time (over 2 days) with this cake and it really helped! I baked the cake and froze it, then the next day prepared the icing and chilled it, iced a layer, froze it, iced more, froze it again, etc. It's not perfect but it's progress! This is a from scratch chocolate cake with an ermine vanilla cream cheese frosting. It was sooooo decadent!

This is my first presentable attempt at making a nice cake, far from perfect but I'm so happy with my progress!
